title: Merge K Sorted Lists
summary: Merge a collection of sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list.

contractDetails.constraints: There are 0–10,000 input lists. Each has at most 500 nodes, and their combined length is at most 10,000. Node values are integers in [−10,000, 10,000]. Each list is nondecreasing.

statement: Merge a collection of sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list. Return its head. Keep every occurrence of each value. Examples show arrays in traversal order.

examples.explanation: All lists contribute, including both copies of 2.
With no input lists, the result is empty.

constraints: There are 0–10,000 input lists. Each has at most 500 nodes, and their combined length is at most 10,000. Node values are integers in [−10,000, 10,000]. Each list is nondecreasing.
hints: Conceptual: Merging two sorted lists at a time can solve the larger problem.
Directional: Pair lists and merge each pair into a new chain, then repeat in rounds.
Implementation: Double the span of each merged block after every round. An unpaired final list advances unchanged.
complexityAnalysis: O(k + N log(max(k,2))) time and O(k) auxiliary space for k lists and N nodes, using a working array of heads.
